meta.data_source: Digital twin simulation (room energy-balance model, heat model v0.1), simulated — not measured. Driven by real SMHI weather (Såtenäs station, 24.7 km away, CC BY 4.0) for a full year, 2025. See data/dashboard-format.md.
meta.scenario_scope: Full year (2025) digital-twin simulation of one real classroom (Room 101, 60.0 m², 25 pupils + 1 teacher) — not a whole-building figure. “Today” (baseline) is the building's actual control faults: 50% of radiator valves stuck open, an outdoor sensor biased -1.5 K low, and a manual 2.0 K morning boost. “Smart control” is coordinated valve control with those faults fixed — the proposed retrofit. Both scenarios share the same weather and occupancy, so the comparison is apples-to-apples.

open_items: Zone size, pupils, gains per person, schedule, radiator size and overheat-purge numbers are placeholders — nothing in the source set pins them down for a Trollhättan school.
SMHI station id for Trollhättan is not resolved yet.
Solar radiation source is not verified (SMHI STRÅNG candidate, Open-Meteo fallback) — the simulated Q_solar term is a synthetic winter-sun stand-in until that's wired up.
Design outdoor temperature (−16 °C) comes from the Gothenburg survey — confirm the Trollhättan value.
TRV motion speed and heat meter specs were not found.
R and C (envelope resistance/heat capacity) are heat-model placeholders — the model owner still needs to define them from the actual building construction.
Whether the heat model or the twin owns Q_solar and Q_vent is undecided per the room-energy-balance contract — agree before the real model replaces this placeholder.
Most Swedish school figures trace back to one 2011 SKR report summarising a 2006 survey — cite the originals (Energimyndigheten STIL2, Jangsten 2017) in the final report.

The twin file (data/twin_dashboard.json) also includes daily/weekly/monthly pre-aggregated series and two more scenarios ("Faults fixed" alone, "Smart control on old valves") that this dashboard doesn't chart yet — see data/dashboard-format.md for the full shape if a resolution switcher or a 4-way scenario comparison gets built later.

The heat-usage forecast card is illustrative only — generated from the twin's own totals as a stand-in, not real model output. The actual model (features, horizons, training data) is described by a teammate but not yet trained/connected; swap data["forecast"] for real output once it exists.

forecast.status_note: Illustrative placeholder, not model output. The forecasting model is still being trained and tuned by the team — these numbers are derived from the twin's own recent totals so the UI slot is grounded in real magnitudes, not from a trained predictor.
forecast.trained_on: ~200k cleaned hourly readings (from 2.2M raw) across 48 Oslo school buildings — SINTEF COFACTOR-SBHUB Oslo dataset (Lien et al., Data in Brief, 2025)
